# @dsh-external/dsh-annotation-patched
English | 中文
## Summary
`dsh-annotation-patched` v0.3.7 adds selection annotation to the DSH Web client. Select text in an a
ssistant reply, write an optional note, and press Enter to send the annotation block with your messa
ge. The model answers each annotation by number, and every numbered answer becomes a hoverable chip
that shows the quoted passage. Pending annotations are stored per session, so they survive a page re
load until you send or delete them.
## Installation
Install the package into the web profile from GitHub:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
To install from a local checkout, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and ad
a local checkout, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and add the directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The profile applies bundle changes at startup. Restart DSH after adding the package, then hard reloa
d the Web page with Ctrl+F5 so the browser fetches the current client bundle.
The package targets the Web client. Its Node entry registers the plugin identity with an empty `appl
y`, and the browser half loads through the client module table.
## Usage
1. Select text in an assistant reply. A small floating toolbar appears next to the selection with a

single **Annotate** button (引用 in the Chinese UI).
2. Click the button. Write a note, or leave it em

pty to quote the passage without a note, then save.
3. The quoted text gets a numbered highlight, an
d a badge above the composer shows `Annotations ×N`. Hover the badge to review the list, click a num

ber to edit its note, and delete entries from the editor.
4. Send with Enter, the send button, or Ct
rl+Enter while the conversation is running. The plugin prepends the annotation block to your message

before the host submits it.
5. The model is asked to answer `Annotation 1` through `Annotation N`.
When the reply finishes streaming, each label becomes a hoverable chip that shows the quoted passage

and your note.
6. A slash skill such as `/human-writing fix this` keeps the annotations. The plugin
appends the annotation block after the command, and the host still loads the skill from the message
. Built-in slash commands such as `/goal` and `/model` send without annotations; a toast says the an
notations stay pending for the next message.
Pending annotations are stored per session in the browser and restored after a reload. Sending clear
s them, and deleting an entry in the badge editor removes it from the pending list.
## Configuration
The plugin reads its settings from the host and the profile entry.
- Display language follows the DSH locale service. Both `zh` and `en` are available, and the plugin
falls back to `zh` when the locale service is absent. The annotation block uses the same language as

the UI.
- Pending annotations live in browser `localStorage` under `dsh.annotation.pending.v1.<sess

ionId>`.
- To disable the plugin, remove the package from the profile, or disable its loader entry i
d `dsh-annotation-patched` in the profile patch layer.
## How the plugin works
Implementation details (click to expand)
`index.mjs` is the Node half. It exports the package name and an empty `apply`; the real work happen
e Node half. It exports the package name and an empty `apply`; the real work happens in the browser.
`client.js` is a hand written CommonJS bundle wrapped in `window.__ModuleLoader__.load`. The registr
ation id must equal the package name. The bundle renders its own DOM and imports no `@deepseek-ai` v
alues. It receives `sessions`, `conversation`, and `locale` as cordis services.
`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the loader entry `dsh-annotation-patched` with `name` set to the package
name. The id differs from the upstream `dsh-annotation` id so both packages can be installed at once
. Later profile patches can override or disable the entry by id.
Selection capture: `selectionchange` opens the toolbar. Saving a quote records the message anchor ke
y, the text offset, the surrounding context, the quoted text, and the note. The pending list is writ
ten to `localStorage` per session, and the source passage is decorated with an absolutely positioned
highlight and number badge.
[该节后续省略]
## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- Only assistant replies can be annotated. Text in user messages is not selectable for annotation.
-
The plugin depends on DSH Web DOM attributes such as `[data-chat-flow-kind="assistant-step"]`, `[da
ta-composer-card]`, `[data-composer-input]`, and `[data-chat-anchor-key]`. A UI change can break sel

ection, attachment, or chip decoration.
- With more than one composer on screen, for example an Agen
t Teams panel or an embedded subagent view, the plugin refuses to attach annotations and sends the m

essage unchanged. It cannot tell which session a composer belongs to.
- Slash skills need the `remot
e.skills` list. When the service is absent, the list has not arrived, or the fetch fails, that messa
ge is sent without annotations and the annotations stay pending. Built-in slash commands never carry

annotations and show a toast instead.
- Inline think stripping matches literal `<think>`, `<thinkin
g>`, `<thought>`, and `<reasoning>` tags in text nodes. When the host renders a tag as HTML and only

the reasoning text remains, the plugin has nothing to match.
- Pending annotations are stored in br
owser `localStorage`. They do not sync across browsers or devices, and clearing site data removes th

em.
- The annotation number, reply chip, and tip layers sit above the Agent Teams panel (z-index 110
). With that panel open they can overlap its top edge and take clicks. Correcting the stacking needs

an `elementFromPoint` occlusion check and real browser verification, so it is deferred.
- When the
current session id cannot be resolved, the plugin leaves the draft untouched and logs one `[annotati

on]` warning. Attachment and cleanup are unavailable for that send.
- `npm test` needs Node >= 22.22
.2 because jsdom 30 declares that range. `engines.node >= 20` covers the DSH host runtime rather tha
0 declares that range. `engines.node >= 20` covers the DSH host runtime rather than the test runner.
